text: Don't be that guy, don't leave a negative review after being like 100 hours in, and you don't like the most minor of a detail about this masterpiece of a game. I beg you, this game has 100% positive reviews for a reason mate.

This feels like a very clever evolution of the "Luck be a Landlord" like gameplay.  You're given a small amount of space (an omelet) to add ingredients to, 1 at a time from your deck of ingredients.  At each turn you'll need to choose 1 of 3 of your collection of ingredients in which you need to factor things like positioning, how the various ingredients put in the omelet so far will work with this new ingredient, any weird mechanics introduced this round by your customer, the customer's side objective, and finally, if all of this wasn't enough, the ingredients you're choosing from are being offered on a moving conveyor belt, so you'll need to decide quickly!  In between each round you'll get to visit a shop where you can buy new ingredients, tools, or other tricks to aid in fulfilling the demands of your next customer (very reminiscent of the shop between rounds in Balatro).

I have bought many games the past year, and I always end up coming back to this game. And I haven't even played all the games I bought! ^^' This game satisfies my urge for roguelike deckbuilders and cooking games which is a combo I never knew I needed in my life until now. 

The pixel art is cute and perfect, and the music is fitting despite being minimal (could probably add more music tracks). It's very challenging so patience even if hard. The animations and unlocking each new run makes the challenges even more exciting. 

The weekly runs are a huge plus in this game and I find myself playing to see where I land on the scoreboard (#89 on the current weekly run, going to see if I can get even higher >:D). The weekly runs force you to be creative with ingredients and placement on omelet in ways you probably would have not thought of doing the base game runs. The weekly runs help keep the game fresh so you aren't just finished when you complete the base game runs. In fact, I still have to beat all the base game runs and I'm almost at 20 hours of playtime! So this game is definitely worth the price for how much you get out of it. 

So, if you like cute roguelite deckbuilders and cooking games, look no further and just buy this game right now! :D  I promise you you won't regret it (okay, maybe a little when serving principal or loan shark lol)

I must admit, this is one of the top games I've ever played. Pixel style games aren't really my preference, but it's playability totally threw that off for me.  
 
·With a great sense of humour, this is more than simply playing memes. The game incorporates a large number of everyday ingredients, but pairs them with unique and hilarious models, effects and actions. 
·Difficulty is divided into a very wide range of degrees from easy to hard, suitable for all casual and competitive players. (The only negative is that with so many difficulties and levels, trying to reach the Platinum Achievement is a very time consuming task. If completing the high difficulty while automatically going completely low should be something I'd like to see ......) 
·The updates are very frequent and you can see that it's not just the chefs who are motivated, but the production team as well. Maybe it's a virtuous climb? 
·Perfectly localised translation, at least in Simplified Chinese. Praise the translation team. 
·I've gained 3kg thanks to spending a lot of time playing this game every night and eating late night snacks (no spanners in them). 
 
In short, make sure you experience this game. Not much more to say, I still have the Platinum Achievement to work on :)

Overall, a really good papa's pizzaria-like game, with elements of balatro that make it so much fun to make your omelette's the best they can be, even if they spelled it wrong in the title :)

And with this review, there is now 500 reviews of this game on steam, all of them positive, I am very proud to be number 500, and to be a part of a very friendly, fun community.

"Omelet You Cook" is a cooking roguelike in which you play as the new canteen chef in Principal Clucker's school. The principal is a picky eater and expects high standards from you, so don't disappoint him!

The main gameplay is heaviliy inspired by Balatro. Every round you have to serve one member of the students or staff of the school. In order to satisfy your customer you have to place various ingredients from your pantry on the omelet you serve. These ingredients give you points and each ingredient has their own scoring mechanics. Some give you just some flat points, other give you more or less points depending if they touch another ingredient. Some ingredients can be placed under or on top of your ingredients, some "point" at something to give you a bonus and some simply earn you money. These ingredients are dispensed randomly on a conveyor belt and you have to pick one from a choice of three up. The game has two modes for this, a turn based mode in which you can take your time to pick up  afood and a real time mode in whioch the ingredients that have been dispensed slowly move to the left until they fall of the conveyor. This means players have to make quick decisions.
You can always move your ingredients around on the plate until you are happy unless a customer has a trait that disallows this. Fantastic game! Waited until 1.0 to start playing, and boy howdy is there a lot of content to be had! I enjoy the moving conveyor belt, it adds tension and chaos to each decision you make. The tiers of difficulty and varying food synergies are engaging. I wish there were features to make steam deck gameplay more cohesive, like adjusting cursor movement and zoom, but playing on the PC is seamless.

One of the freshest experiences in the deluge of new games constantly coming out.

As I roll credits on beating the final boss for the first time (with plenty of content left to explore and achievements to unlock), I just had to rush over here to highly recommend this game. It's super fun, has a ton of depth with seemingly endless synergies and build customization, a playful art style, catchy music, and devs who really put their all in this game - seriously, you can message a dev and they'll respond extremely quickly. They are constantly updating the game, tweaking features, adding helpers/ingredients/achievements, etc. The player community is super cool and helpful too, if you have any questions.

If you like roguelikes, the idea of "food Balatro," or food at all, don't delay your purchase any longer.

I feel like I'm barely scratching the surface of this game and it won't [i] spoil [/i] any time soon.
Extremely good for short bursts of gaming and to kill time. Devs fix things (it's early access after all!) timely and give a lot of feedback. Definetely reccomended!

An absolutely delightfully silly cooking Balatro-like.

There's nothing like serving kids a flaming bag of trash and a couple of fish bones and getting paid for it.

It's 2am and I am doing one more omelet to feed to a giant chicken. 10/10 would omelet again.

To be more precise it's got all the charm of Balatro but it's live action game where you have to make split second decisions. 

Difficulty also ramps up nicely the longer you play so the gameplay loop keeps being challenging and there's alot of things to unlock and achievements to hunt.

This is a good rogue-like; had a lot of fun with it.  
 
Multiple characters to choose from as you progress each with their own "deck" of ingredients. You earn money and can purchase new items (adding modifiers) or ingredients to your "deck" that combo and interact with each other in various ways. 
 
The core gameplay is placing the ingredients in the most point advantageous way to progress through each round. Kept coming back to it and never got frustrated with it.

Super fun Balatro-esque by way of chaos omelettes. Supremely satisfying figuring out how the ingredients synergise together (shoutouts to the UI design for giving a good way of figuring out what will and won't work together at a glance), and just the right amount of absurdity in what it'll let you put on an omelette.

It's easy to pick up and a simple concept, but it can certainly rack up difficulty in the right ways and they put many interesting and unique twists on all the ingredients and customers. The only thing that I can think of which is close to a complaint is that there's no way to access achievements from within the game; it would be nice if the achievements were in the catalogue along with all the customers and ingredients which could help or hinder getting a certain goal. Well, I guess I would also like a way to access the flavor text that Principal Clucker gives when accessing brand new ingredients in the game; lore isn't too important for the game and that's fine, but I would like to see how far I had to go to get to my endgame status, if only out of my own curiosity,

I can say that the devs here did it right for sure, great creative thinking all around.

This is the best roguelike I've personally played! There's just so much here for something so simple! Great 2D artwork, fun gameplay with endless replayability! And for those completionists that want to get all the achievements, this game is very fun to 100%! I've gotten all 112 achievements, and it was a blast the whole way through!

9/10, a must play for any roguelike fan!
